{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOLEgSIs8AAAABXr3bfQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm7fazhBQHqk", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm7fa", "number": 13, "title": "Implement WebXR DOM Overlay for Android AR and Quest 3 MR", "body": "## Problem

The WebXR emulator currently reports `dom-overlay` as unsupported for both supported device profiles. In `src/polyfill/api/runtime.ts`, `XRSession.domOverlayState` always returns `null`; `EmulatedXRDevice.isFeatureSupported()` does not enable `dom-overlay`. Old `domOverlayRoot` / `z-index` logic remains in `EmulatedXRDevice.ts`, but it does not implement correct immersive DOM presentation or XR/DOM interaction. This outstanding portion of [Issue #11](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/issues/11) was explicitly left incomplete by the partial [PR #12](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/pull/12).

The emulator already has a Three.js-powered handheld Android AR phone display and stereo Quest 3 MR compositor, but DOM Overlay requires browser-rendered HTML/CSS to be visibly composited **inside the emulated XR view**, with correct hit testing, events, and security boundaries. A desktop-only floating `z-index` layer is not sufficient.

## Expected outcome

Support the [WebXR DOM Overlays Module](https://www.w3.org/TR/2024/WD-webxr-dom-overlays-1-20240924/) in the existing **Generic Android Phone (ARCore) immersive AR** and **Meta Quest 3 immersive MR** simulations, without implying native XR compositor control or physical-device fidelity.

- **Android:** Present a usable, interactive `screen` overlay aligned with the simulated phone XR viewport (including phone movement/resizing as applicable).
- **Quest MR:** Present an interactive overlay perceptible in the stereo headset views, using an accurately described `head-locked` or `floating` mode according to the *actual implemented* projection. Correct per-eye placement, transforms, visibility and input-ray intersections matter more than merely displaying the DOM somewhere on the desktop.
- Correctly implement `domOverlay.root` and `requiredFeatures`/`optionalFeatures` negotiation, `XRSession.domOverlayState`, `beforexrselect`, DOM pointer/click behavior, and lifecycle cleanup, while protecting cross-origin content.

The goal is a **useful standards-aligned simulator**, not an unsupported assertion of full user-agent rendering/CSS conformance. Because a browser extension cannot necessarily implement native UA-owned `:xr-overlay` styling or faithful arbitrary HTML/iframe-to-stereo-texture capture, these limitations must be investigated and demonstrated. **Never advertise `dom-overlay` for a profile/mode unless it has a usable, tested view-and-input implementation.** If a required target proves infeasible, document the technical blocker, leave that acceptance item unmet and the Issue open rather than claiming complete support.

## Context

- Follow the repository [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/development-flow.md), [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/review-guidelines.md), and Issue/PR templates; use English for collaboration content. Start from and target `dev`.
- Relevant code: `src/polyfill/api/runtime.ts` (XRSession and feature negotiation/input events), `src/polyfill/EmulatedXRDevice.ts` (presentation canvas, legacy overlay remnants, XR input), `src/polyfill/ARScene.ts` (phone surface, Quest two-eye compositor, renderer raycasts), `src/polyfill/api/layers.ts`, `src/types/polyfill.ts`, `src/app/panel.ts`, `tests/conformance.ts`, and `tests/browser-smoke.ts`.
- The current profiles are **Meta Quest 3** (VR/MR toggle) and **Generic Android Phone (ARCore)**. Focus on their **immersive-ar** configurations; do not misrepresent inline/VR as DOM Overlay-supported. Preserve existing hit tests, Anchors, Layers, Depth Sensing, Hand Input and Lighting Estimation functionality, with correct interactions between enabled features.
- The W3C DOM Overlay module is a **Working Draft dated 24 September 2024**, not a final Recommendation. Verify the current revision at implementation time and cite the specific normative requirements chosen. Relevant sections cover [the `:xr-overlay` pseudo-class](https://www.w3.org/TR/2024/WD-webxr-dom-overlays-1-20240924/#css-pseudo-class), [session integration](https://www.w3.org/TR/2024/WD-webxr-dom-overlays-1-20240924/#webxr-device-api-integration), [`beforexrselect`](https://www.w3.org/TR/2024/WD-webxr-dom-overlays-1-20240924/#onbeforexrselect) and [cross-origin handling](https://www.w3.org/TR/2024/WD-webxr-dom-overlays-1-20240924/#event-handling-for-cross-origin-content).
- Preserve packaged Manifest V3 MAIN-world synchronous injection, isolated privileged messaging and CSP restrictions. No remote code, `eval`, unsafe arbitrary HTML serialization, permission bypass or XR data leakage into cross-origin frames.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] **Research and document rendering feasibility** for the real browser rendering of DOM, CSS and event targets over (a) the handheld phone's 3D screen and (b) Quest MR stereo views. Implement and exercise at least one concrete prototype in the automated browser environment, document rejected alternatives (e.g. arbitrary DOM-to-texture capture), and explain any fundamental CSS `:xr-overlay`/UA-compositor limitations. Do not equate a visually separate desktop overlay with in-headset rendering.
- [ ] **Feature negotiation:** Support `dom-overlay` only for the applicable, working immersive modes. Validate `domOverlay.root` (required Element, valid document/ownership where applicable) and required/optional feature combinations with correct error and promise behavior; unsupported required features reject and unsupported optional features are omitted. `session.enabledFeatures` and `session.domOverlayState` reflect actual support; returned `type` is a stable `screen`, `head-locked` or `floating` value matching actual geometry for the duration of the session.
- [ ] **Android rendering:** Show actual styled, interactive overlay content within the simulated phone AR viewport. Test transparency, correct foreground layering above XR scene content, content placement, clipping, viewport matching under high DPI/resize, phone/camera movement and overlay activation from the start of the session. Support representative native HTML controls and scrolling to the extent legitimately possible.
- [ ] **Quest MR rendering:** Display readable, interactive DOM Overlay content in both eyes of the Quest MR view with appropriate stereo disparity/head-locked or floating placement, consistent per-eye coordinates on viewport/DPR/resize changes, and correct layering above the emulated XR imagery. Do not report a supported Quest overlay if it is only visible on the unrelated desktop page.
- [ ] **DOM/CSS behavior:** Use real browser DOM/CSS where possible; preserve overlay root identity, descendant layout and focus. Verify expected fixed transparent overlay styling and style restoration at session end. Evaluate `:xr-overlay` behavior with a real stylesheet/test; if the native selector cannot be provided by an extension, document the incompatibility accurately and avoid presenting custom-class styling as full CSS-conformant behavior.
- [ ] **Input integration:** Hit-test pointer/touch/controller target rays against the displayed overlay and dispatch the bubbling, composed, cancelable `beforexrselect` with an appropriate `XRSessionEvent` and topmost target. When cancelled, suppress the corresponding `selectstart`, `selectend` and `select` sequence without breaking `inputsourceschange` or unrelated interactions. When not cancelled, preserve XR Select behavior. DOM pointer/click/focus interactions must still work independently; test both Quest controllers and phone transient `screen` input, including input beginning/ending in an overlay and event ordering.
- [ ] **Cross-origin protection:** Investigate and implement a spec-permitted policy for cross-origin iframes inside an overlay (prefer blocking their XR-derived interaction when pose/gamepad limiting cannot be faithfully implemented). Ensure no cross-origin frame obtains XR controller poses/gamepad state or clickjacking-prone synthesized XR events. Cover same-origin DOM descendants, cross-origin iframe targets, and transitions into/out of cross-origin regions in tests. State and test any supported restrictions.
- [ ] **Lifecycle and integration:** Correct cleanup on `XRSession.end()`, switching Quest VR/MR or devices, reloading the page, moving/removing/replacing the overlay element, visibility changes, and worker restart. Restore changed inline styles/DOM positioning, avoid leaked listeners/textures, and preserve the existing WebXR layer compositor, AR hit tests and session input behavior.
- [ ] **Automated verification:** Add focused assertions to `tests/conformance.ts` plus an end-to-end sample in `tests/browser-smoke.ts` (or a dedicated script). Include required/optional negotiation, `domOverlayState`, real DOM interaction, event cancellation and ordering, normal and cross-origin UI, both profiles/modes, DPI/resize/viewport, teardown/restart, negative cases and CSP. Use screenshots/pixel or perceptual assertions to verify overlay placement in actual simulated XR imagery; record known gaps.
- [ ] Run and record actual results of `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run build:firefox`, `npm run test:browser`, and relevant conformance/WPT/sample checks on a contemporary desktop Chromium. Distinguish checks that were not run or browser limitations from passes. Optional Firefox runtime results must not be invented.
- [ ] Update README, `docs/webxr-conformance.md` and validation notes with verified profile/mode support, overlay types, browser/CSS security limitations and reproducible tests. **Do not mark this Issue complete unless both Android AR and Quest MR display/input requirements are satisfied**; partial PRs may be merged only while describing remaining work accurately, without closing this Issue.
- [ ] Open the implementation PR(s) against `dev` using the repository template, request review and report real test results, failures and known limitations.

## Optional validation

- Run tests on Firefox's separately packaged MV3 extension if a supported runtime is available.
- Exercise published WebXR DOM Overlay sample applications and more complex responsive HTML/CSS controls, including keyboard/focus/accessibility behavior.
- Investigate native-browser alternatives or collaboration with browser engine implementers for aspects that cannot be emulated without UA support.

## Required post-merge verification

None. All mandatory rendering, event, security, regression and documentation checks should occur before merge; browser-store publication and hardware certification are not part of this Issue.
